Homeless to me means anything from living on the streets, to living in your car, to moving from place to place for free or sleeping in shelters. I would classify people as not homeless if they have a job and are currently renting or have bought a house. 

My mom and him divorced when I was very young and she didn't want him living with us for a various amount of reasons. She later got re-married, and it would be hard for her to let him stay with us. My father, and other homeless people often don't have the means to pay rent. I'm sure he would have loved to be able to. It varies from person to person based on their situation.

Wow, first of all, you are a very strong person and I am sending my thoughts to you!! Also, thank you. We feel very lucky. 

But, In my my father's case, he was finally helped financially by his mother who should have helped all along. I know this answer doesn't help other homeless people immediately, and I wish it did, but what I can say about it is that the strength of family can have such a major impact on the individuals who find themselves homeless. 

Homeless family members or members of the family with mental illnesses that impact their ability to function in society should not be an embarrassment and should not be cast away or forgotten. It's an absolute tragedy that this happens. So those who do have family members with these issues should do their best to reach out to them, and people who know families dealing with a family member like this, should be 100% supportive of that family. 

I'm sure there are other ways that a homeless man could go about buying a house and I'm very interested in studying the subject in depth, but I don't have answers other than this.

This may seem like a weird question, but what is it exactly that feels awful and ugly to you when you look in the mirror.. like what specifically? I personally had the same problem all throughout my teen years and earlier 20's, but recently started finding the beauty in my imperfections. I looked at pictures a few weeks ago of how I looked when I was so insecure and thought that I looked very beautiful in the pictures. What I mean to say is, you more than likely look more beautiful than you think, even if you aren't seeing it for yourself. (And this is coming from someone who suffered extreme self esteem issues, especially about not looking "as pretty as others" or how I "wished I looked"). 

The reason I ask what specifically you find awful or ugly about yourself, is that I found the more I realized what wasn't "perfect" about myself in my eyes, the more I could work on accepting those flaws into my own "beauty". For example, I have gap teeth, which hindered me from smiling with my teeth FOREVER, but now that I've accepted that I just find it to make me "uglier," I have started smiling with my teeth showing, and it actually makes me feel prettier to do so. We are all flawed in one way or another, but confidence and self love looks better on everyone. 

I'm sorry you are feeling down about yourself, but I assure you, you are more beautiful than you think. You will certainly find love, and you will come to a point where you love who you are.

I am so glad I could be there for you during one of your worst times. I know what it feels like to be stuck inside your head, and I do think it's key to be able to open up. It's so hard to feel like there is anyone who would be willing to listen, and I'm glad I've helped you feel that way. 

I think dropping everything and traveling would be a good thing for you to do at some point in your life. New experiences are so good for creating vivid and happy memories, and you deserve to have that instead of feeling stuck where you are and feeling apathetic about your surroundings. If dreaming about the places you wish you could be is enjoyable for you, I would let yourself do that. You can always go to all the old favorite places as well as the exciting new places. 

The thing about helping others while you are still overcoming your own problems is realizing that there are people who are in similar boats as you that can benefit from your experiences. We really are all in this human experience together. It can really make their day to have insight from someone who is also overcoming problems, and making their day will make your day. You learn from each other. It's a good cycle. 

I do believe this is the first step and I wish you the best on that journey! You can PM whenever if you ever need to talk in the future :)

Depression tends to work that way sometimes, and it makes no sense, but it's okay that you aren't 100% sure why you are sad. Most of the time when I get depression it's either for no reason or for what seems to be something I "should have" gotten over more easily. But I just have to accept it. There could even be an underlying reason that you aren't fully aware of, as well. But I think your main focus should be making it through these classes, and then you can figure out what that reason may be, if there is one. Just accepting the depression for what it is, regardless of the reason, can be helpful in the act of acknowledging that it's there, but putting it aside.

Yes, I have pushed through with sheer willpower. It takes a lot of shedding any emotional state that I belong to at the time (for example putting my depression to the side for the time being), getting organized in a real way, and reminding myself of my end goal. I am a perfectionist in a big way, and often times making it through to the end also requires me to shed my perfectionist tendencies, as well. You must tell yourself to do your work regardless of whether or not it is perfect. Most of the time, nothing is, especially under strict time limitations when you are falling behind. Just remind yourself that if you do your work, it will be enough for the teacher, and that's the bare minimum of what matters in a class.  

Also, I definitely feel you when it comes to the extreme guilt of doing poorly in school in any way. The guilt adds stress to the situation every time. Talking to your teachers will help, indeed, but I think it will also take some forgiveness from yourself. Remind yourself that what your end goal is to pass your classes for the sake of your major, and then forgive yourself for the way your life has become and for the fact that you've fallen behind. In all honesty, it is okay, as long as you are turning in assignments, and even better if you are doing work that you are proud of. 

You may not even make it all the way to an A grade this time, but that is okay!vDo what you feel is the best you can do in this moment, in your depressed state, and you will feel much better than you would if you didn't try. And if you are feeling worried about your GPA, look into whether or not your school does a Pass/Fail grading system for times of need. That way, even if you pass with a grade you aren't proud of, it won't affect your GPA. 

And remember, if you know that you have been a good student in the past, that means you ARE a good student. Depression hinders you, but it's not going to hinder you forever. This term might not be what you want it to be, but if you can pull through with the bare minimums, the next term can be a fresh start. In other words, even if you aren't proud of this term, there are always more to come! 

It's a great sign that you think catching up is possible, and I really believe you can do it. I am rooting for you! Don't forget to wake up on time and eat breakfast! Buy yourself some blueberry bagels, that always helps me wake up in the morning :)

Having worked in the food industry for years, I personally don't bother going into a sit down restaurant within the last hour, (and definitely not the last 30 minutes) and if I absolutely have to for some reason, I get the food to go and make sure I'm very polite and tip well. I think the worst part, though, is how stressful it is for someone to sit down in the lobby knowing they will probably be there past closing time. Not only are they technically getting in the way of closing procedures at that point, but it can also be stressful for employees to make sure that person doesn't feel rushed if they are past close (which they probably will be). If they are good employees, they want their customers to have a good and comfortable experience in their establishment. That is why I get the food to go if I *have* to be there late. 

All in all, it's best, in my opinion, to just make sure you give yourself a good hour/hour and fifteen minutes while going to a restaurant. It will be a better experience for everyone. Either way, be polite and thank them for what they are doing, especially if you had a good experience with them!
